script:
You are a professional screenwriter.

Write a modern screenplay.

Constraints:
- No guns
- No gun violence
- No weapon combat
- No graphic violence
- No copyrighted characters
- Completely original story

Requirements:
- 10–15 scenes
- Proper screenplay format
- INT/EXT scene headers
- Dialogue in uppercase character format
- Realistic pacing

Genre: Workplace
Theme: forgiveness

Begin screenplay.

Title: "THE HEALING HANDS"

INT. HEALING HANDS CLINIC - DAY

A bustling clinic filled with patients and staff. RECEPTIONIST JANE, mid-30s, greets patients warmly as they enter. NURSE SARA, late-20s, prepares a room for the next patient.

INT. PATIENT ROOM - DAY

DR. LUCAS, 40s, enters the room, carrying a clipboard. He greets the patient, OLIVIA, early 30s, with a kind smile.

DR. LUCAS
(cheerfully)
Good morning, Olivia. How are you today?

OLIVIA
(sighs)
Same old pain, Doctor.

Dr. Lucas listens sympathetically, taking notes.

INT. HEALING HANDS CLINIC - RECEPTION AREA - DAY

Jane greets a NEW PATIENT, GABRIEL, mid-20s, with a warm smile. He looks uneasy.

JANE
(encouragingly)
Don't worry, Mr. Gabriel. Dr. Lucas is the best in the business. He'll take good care of you.

INT. PATIENT ROOM - DAY

Dr. Lucas examines a new patient, ISABELLA, late 40s, with a gentle touch.

ISABELLA
(tearfully)
I don't want to be a burden to anyone.

DR. LUCAS
(reassuringly)
You're not a burden, Isabella. You deserve to live a pain-free life. Let's work together to make that happen.

INT. HEALING HANDS CLINIC - RECEPTION AREA - DAY

Sara talks to a worried PATIENT, MARK, late 30s.

SARA
(supportively)
I understand how difficult this is for you, Mark. But remember, Dr. Lucas and our team are here to help you through this.

INT. PATIENT ROOM - DAY

Dr. Lucas comforts a FAMILY, MOTHER and TWO CHILDREN, who've come for a checkup.

DR. LUCAS
(smiling)
You all look well. I'm glad to see you're all doing great.

INT. HEALING HANDS CLINIC - BREAK ROOM - DAY

Sara and Jane chat over lunch.

SARA
(whispering)
I've noticed Dr. Lucas seems exhausted lately. Do you know what's going on?

JANE
(concerned)
No, but I'll make sure to check on him.

INT. PATIENT ROOM - DAY

Dr. Lucas talks to a depressed patient, JACK, early 50s.

DR. LUCAS
(gently)
You're not alone, Jack. We'll get through this together.

INT. HEALING HANDS CLINIC - RECEPTION AREA - DAY

Jane greets a regular patient, MARY, late 50s, who brings flowers for the reception area.

JANE
(delighted)
Thank you so much, Mary. Our patients love these.

INT. PATIENT ROOM - DAY

Dr. Lucas checks up on a recovering patient, JENNY, mid-20s, who's been in a car accident. She's visibly anxious.

JENNY
(nervously)
Am I going to be okay?

DR. LUCAS
(confidently)
Yes, Jenny. You're going to be just fine.

INT. HEALING HANDS CLINIC - RECEPTION AREA - END OF DAY

Staff clean up the clinic and prepare for the next day. Dr. Lucas enters, looking worn but determined.

DR. LUCAS
(exhausted)
Another long day. But it's all worth it to help these people.

INT. HEALING HANDS CLINIC - NIGHT

As everyone leaves, Sara approaches Dr. Lucas.

SARA
(concerned)
Are you okay, Dr. Lucas? You seem so tired.

DR. LUCAS
(sighs)
It's been a long day. But I'll be fine. I have to be strong for my patients.

Sara wraps her arms around him in a comforting hug.

SARA
(softly)
You don't have to do this alone, Dr. Lucas. We're all here to help you.

They share a moment of understanding, knowing that forgiveness and support can heal even the deepest wounds.

FADE OUT.
